prompts.article:
You write customer support articles for Halvard Home, an invented maker of home appliances.
Write one support article about the product and topic below. Start with a short title line,
then the article, 100 to 140 words, in plain UK English. The article must state one specific,
concrete fact clearly, such as a setting, a duration, a figure, a step, or a cause, so a
reader could answer a question from it. Do not mention any error code or part number other
than one given below.
prompts.identifier:
The article is about {kind} {identifier}. Use exactly "{identifier}" once, and say clearly
what it means for this product and what to do. Invent a fault that fits the topic.

questions.paraphrase:
Here is a support article. Write one question a customer might ask whose answer is the
article's key fact. Use completely different words from the article: everyday phrasing and
synonyms, and no word that appears in the article, apart from very common words such as
"the", "how", or "my". Reply with the question only.
questions.shared:
Here is a support article. Write one question a customer might ask whose answer is the
article's key fact, using the article's own key words, including the product name. Reply
with the question only.
questions.retry:
Your question broke the rule. {problem} Write a new question that follows the rule. Reply
with the question only.

articles.text:
Resetting your Ashby tumble dryer

On the Ashby tumble dryer, E-2194 means a factory reset was interrupted before the saved settings could be cleared. Your previous preferences may still be active.

To try the reset again:

1. Switch the dryer off, unplug it and wait five minutes.
2. Check that the drum is empty, then close the door.
3. Plug the dryer back in and switch it on without selecting a programme.
4. Press and hold the Temperature and Delay Start buttons together for ten seconds.
5. Release both buttons when the display shows “Reset”, then wait until the programme selection screen returns.

A completed reset clears saved drying preferences and delayed starts. If the warning returns, stop repeating the reset and contact Halvard Home support.

Child lock warning on your Orrin heat pump

On the Orrin heat pump, E-1294 means the child lock button has been detected as continuously pressed, so the control panel remains locked. Moisture or dirt on the touch panel can cause this warning.

To clear it:

- Remove anything resting against the control panel.
- Wipe the panel with a soft, dry cloth. Do not spray cleaner directly onto it.
- Make sure your hands are dry, then press and hold the child lock button for five seconds.

When the lock symbol disappears, the controls are available again. The heat pump keeps its previous heating setting while locked.

If the warning returns, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the casing or attempt to repair the controls yourself.

Keel washing machine: child lock will not release

On the Halvard Home Keel washing machine, E-4194 means the child lock has failed to release after you switched it off. The control buttons remain locked because the machine has not confirmed that the lock is disabled.

To reset the child lock:

1. Press and hold the Child Lock button for three seconds.
2. If the lock symbol stays lit, switch the machine off at the socket and unplug it for two minutes.
3. Reconnect the power, switch the machine on, then hold Child Lock for three seconds again.

The child lock disables the controls; it does not indicate whether the door is safe to open. Never force the door. If the controls remain locked, contact Halvard Home support.

articles.topic: the app not finding the device
articles.text:
Ashby tumble dryer not appearing in the app

If the Halvard Home app cannot find your Ashby tumble dryer, its Wi-Fi module may be stuck in standby. This prevents the dryer from broadcasting its setup signal.

KX-9283 is the part number for the Ashby’s Wi-Fi module, which connects the dryer to the app.

Try these steps:
- Switch the dryer off at the socket for 60 seconds, then switch it back on.
- Connect your phone to your home’s 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.
- Hold the dryer’s Wi-Fi button for five seconds, until its light flashes.
- Open the app and select “Add appliance”.

If the dryer still does not appear, contact Halvard Home support and describe the discovery problem. Do not open the casing or replace the module yourself.

Moving your Brio kettle safely

Before moving your Brio kettle, unplug it, empty all water and let it cool completely. Lift the kettle off its base and dry both items before packing.

Check that the lid closes securely. A loose lid latch can allow the lid to spring open during transport. KX-2983 is the replacement lid latch for the Brio kettle. If the latch is cracked or the lid will not stay shut, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support to arrange replacement. Do not tape the lid shut and continue boiling water.

Wrap the kettle and base separately in soft packing material. Keep both upright in a sturdy box, and never carry the kettle by its cable or lid.

Lumen thermostat child lock

The child lock stops children changing the temperature using the Lumen smart thermostat’s screen. To switch it on, press and hold the padlock symbol for five seconds. A closed padlock confirms that the screen controls are locked. Repeat this step to unlock them.

If the lock switches off without anyone touching the screen, a faulty touch sensor may be registering an unlock command.

KX-1283 is the replacement touch-panel assembly for this product, including the sensor that detects child lock commands. Contact Halvard Home support to arrange inspection and, if needed, replacement. Do not open the thermostat yourself.

Until the fault is fixed, do not rely on the child lock to prevent temperature changes.

Vale fridge freezer: unusual vibration

On the Vale fridge freezer, E-7084 means the vibration sensor has detected excessive movement while the compressor is running. An uneven position or contact with nearby furniture can trigger this fault.

To check the appliance:

- Switch it off at the socket and unplug it.
- Check that bottles, shelves and drawers are secure.
- Make sure the cabinet is not touching a wall or cupboard.
- Check that the fridge freezer stands level. Adjust the front levelling feet if needed, without tipping the appliance.
- Leave it unplugged for five minutes, then reconnect it.

If the vibration or warning returns, contact Halvard Home support. An internal compressor mounting may need attention. Do not remove the rear cover or attempt to tighten internal components.

Updating your Mira robot vacuum

On the Halvard Home Mira robot vacuum, error E-7804 means the firmware download was interrupted before installation could begin. Your vacuum is still using its previous firmware.

To retry the update:

1. Place Mira on its charging dock and leave the dock switched on.
2. Check that your home Wi-Fi is working and that Mira shows as connected in the Halvard Home app.
3. Open Mira’s settings in the app, select ‘Firmware update’, then tap ‘Retry’.
4. Keep the vacuum docked and your router switched on until the app confirms the update is complete.

If the update fails again, close and reopen the app, then retry once. Contact Halvard Home support if the problem continues.

articles.topic: the app not finding the device
articles.text:
Brio kettle not appearing in the app

On the Brio kettle, E-7484 means the wireless pairing window has expired, so the app can no longer discover the kettle. This is a connection issue, not a heating fault.

To reconnect:

1. Place the kettle on its powered base, but do not start boiling.
2. Press and hold the wireless button for five seconds, until its light flashes blue.
3. Open the Halvard Home app and select **Add device** within two minutes.
4. Keep your phone within one metre of the kettle until pairing finishes.

If the kettle still does not appear, enable Bluetooth on your phone and allow the app to find nearby devices. Close and reopen the app, then repeat the pairing steps.

Pairing your Orrin heat pump with a voice assistant

If your voice assistant cannot find your Orrin heat pump, its voice pairing module may have stopped responding. This fault can prevent linking even when control through the Halvard Home app still works.

KX-3107 is the part number for the Orrin’s voice pairing module, not an error message. Try resetting its pairing connection before seeking a repair:

1. Open the Halvard Home app and select your heat pump.
2. Go to Settings, then Voice control, and select Reset pairing.
3. Wait 30 seconds, then select Pair voice assistant.
4. Follow the instructions to link your account again.

If pairing still fails, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the heat pump or attempt to replace the module yourself.

Lumen smart thermostat warranty

Your Halvard Home Lumen smart thermostat has a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. It covers manufacturing faults during normal household use.

KX-3170 is the part number identifying this thermostat. Quote it when contacting Halvard Home support so we can check the correct product’s warranty.

For example, if the display repeatedly goes blank while the thermostat still has power, an internal manufacturing fault may be responsible. Contact support with your proof of purchase, purchase date and a brief description of when the problem occurs.

Do not open the casing or attempt an internal repair. Support will assess the fault and explain the next steps. Accidental damage and normal wear are not covered.

Keel washing machine not switching on

If your Keel washing machine shows no lights and does not respond to the power button, start by checking its power supply.

Make sure the plug is firmly inserted and the wall socket is switched on. Test the socket with a working lamp. If the lamp does not light, have the socket checked by a qualified electrician.

Unplug the washing machine for 60 seconds, then reconnect it and try again.

KX-3100 is the Keel’s internal power switch module. A failed module can stop power reaching the controls, leaving the display dark.

If the socket works but the machine remains off, unplug it and contact Halvard Home support to arrange an inspection. Do not remove the casing or attempt to replace the module yourself.

Connecting your Brio kettle to wi-fi

The Brio kettle connects to a 2.4 GHz home wi-fi network. If your router offers separate networks, choose the 2.4 GHz option rather than 5 GHz.

Before you begin, place the kettle on its powered base and keep your phone nearby. Connect your phone to the network you want the kettle to use.

Open the Halvard Home app, select ‘Add appliance’ and choose ‘Brio kettle’. Follow the prompts to put the kettle into pairing mode, then enter your wi-fi password. Keep the app open until it confirms the connection.

If pairing fails, check the password carefully and move the kettle closer to your router, keeping it on a dry, stable surface. Restart the app before trying again.

articles.topic: using it in a holiday home
articles.text:
Using your Tessa dishwasher in a holiday home

A little preparation helps keep your Tessa dishwasher fresh between visits.

Before leaving, run a wash to clear any dirty dishes. Once the programme has finished, unload the dishwasher and allow the interior to cool. Clean the filter following the instructions in your user manual, then wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth.

If the property will be empty for an extended period, switch off the electricity supply and close the dishwasher’s water supply valve. Leave the door slightly open, where safe, to help moisture escape.

If the home could freeze, ask a qualified installer about draining the appliance before you leave.

On your return, restore both supplies and check for leaks before running a wash.

articles.topic: using it in a holiday home
articles.text:
Using your Ashby dryer in a holiday home

Keep a short set of drying instructions near your Ashby tumble dryer so guests can use it safely and confidently.

Clean the lint filter after every load. A blocked filter restricts airflow and can make drying take longer. Before starting, check clothing care labels and remove anything that is not suitable for tumble drying.

Avoid overloading the drum, and keep the area around the dryer clear so air can circulate. Ask guests to stay in the property while it is running and let the programme finish, including its cooling stage.

Between bookings, check that the drum is empty and the filter is clean. If the holiday home will be empty for an extended period, switch off and unplug the dryer.

Fenwick cooker hood warranty

Your Halvard Home Fenwick cooker hood comes with a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. Keep your receipt or order confirmation, as you will need it to show when you bought the appliance.

The warranty covers faults caused by defective materials or workmanship during normal domestic use. It does not cover accidental damage, misuse or routine maintenance, such as cleaning grease filters.

If your cooker hood develops a fault during the warranty period, contact Halvard Home customer support. Have your proof of purchase ready and describe what is happening. Do not attempt internal repairs yourself; support can advise you on the next steps.

Your warranty does not affect your statutory rights.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Corra induction hob: fault on the display

If your Corra induction hob shows a fault message, stop cooking and switch off the hob using its controls. Remove pans only when it is safe to do so.

Check that the control area is clean and dry, with no cloths, utensils or spills covering it. Allow hot surfaces to cool before wiping them.

To try a reset, switch off the hob at its wall isolator for 60 seconds, then restore power. Only do this if the isolator is safely accessible.

If the message returns, leave the hob switched off and contact Halvard Home support. Note exactly what the display shows and when the fault appears. Do not remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

articles.topic: a fault code on the display
articles.text:
Ashby tumble dryer: fault code on the display

If your Ashby tumble dryer shows a fault code, stop the programme and note exactly what appears on the display.

Switch the dryer off at the wall and unplug it. Wait 5 minutes before reconnecting it. While it is unplugged and cool, remove fluff from the lint filter and check that any accessible air vents are clear. If your dryer has a water container, empty it and refit it securely.

Reconnect the dryer and try starting a programme once. If the code returns, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support with the displayed code and your model details.

Do not remove panels or attempt internal repairs. If you notice smoke or a burning smell, do not restart the dryer.

Frost or condensation in your Tessa dishwasher

Condensation can form when warm, moist air touches cooler surfaces inside the dishwasher. A few droplets on the inner door after a wash are usually normal.

Once the cycle has finished and the dishes have cooled, unload the dishwasher and wipe the inner door with a soft, dry cloth. Leave the door slightly ajar, if safe to do so, to help moisture escape. Keep rinse aid topped up to support drying.

Frost or ice is not normal. If you find ice inside, do not start a programme. Switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Do not use boiling water or a sharp tool to remove ice, as these can damage surfaces and seals.

Burning smell from your Ashby tumble dryer

Stop the dryer immediately if you notice a burning smell. Switch it off and unplug it from the wall socket, but only if it is safe to do so. Do not run another cycle to test it.

If there is smoke or flame, keep the dryer door closed, leave the property and call 999. Do not use water or try to move the appliance.

If there are no signs of fire, leave the dryer unplugged until it has cooled completely. You can then remove fluff from the lint filter and check that external air vents are clear.

A burning smell can indicate overheating or an electrical fault. Do not use the dryer again until a qualified appliance technician has checked it.

Setting a delayed start on your Lumen thermostat

Use the heating schedule on your Halvard Home Lumen smart thermostat to start heating later. Set the time you want heating to begin, rather than the number of minutes you want to wait.

For a one-hour delay at 18:00, set the start time to 19:00. Choose your target temperature, then save the schedule. Check that the schedule is enabled and applies to the correct day.

Heating will only be needed if the room is cooler than your target temperature. If nothing happens at the scheduled time, check the room temperature and the thermostat’s clock.

To change your plans, edit or remove the scheduled start so it does not run unexpectedly.

Unusual vibration from your Keel washing machine

If your Halvard Home Keel washing machine vibrates more than usual, pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop before checking it.

An uneven load can cause vibration during the spin cycle. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items, such as towels, evenly around the drum, then restart the programme. Do not force the door open.

Check that the machine stands firmly on a hard, level floor. All four feet should touch the floor, and the machine should not rock when gently pushed at opposite corners.

If it is newly installed, check the installation guide to confirm the transit bolts were removed.

Stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support if strong vibration continues.

# Water leaking underneath your Keel washing machine

If water is leaking underneath your Keel washing machine, stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap. Switch off and unplug the machine only if the plug and surrounding area are dry. Do not touch a wet socket or plug.

Once it is safe, wipe up the water and check these possible sources without moving the machine:

- Look for drips at any visible inlet hose connections.
- Check whether the drain hose has slipped out of its drain.
- Look for water running down from the detergent drawer. Too much detergent can create excess foam and cause leaks.

Do not run another cycle while the leak remains unexplained. If the hoses appear secure or water comes from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support.

Installing your Ashby tumble dryer

Before installing your Halvard Home Ashby tumble dryer, read the supplied installation instructions and check that your chosen space meets the clearance requirements.

Remove all packaging from inside and around the drum. Place the dryer on a firm, level floor, then adjust its feet until it sits steadily without rocking. Keep ventilation openings clear of carpets and other obstructions.

Follow the supplied instructions for any vent hose or water drainage connection required by your model. Plug the dryer directly into a suitable earthed wall socket; do not use an extension lead.

Wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth before first use. If the cable is damaged or you are unsure about the electrical supply, do not connect the dryer. Seek qualified help.

Mira robot vacuum leaking underneath

If water collects underneath your Mira robot vacuum, stop cleaning and switch it off. If the charging dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and look for cracks around the tank and its outlet. A loose filler cap can allow water to escape.

Wipe the tank and the underside of the vacuum with a dry cloth. Do not rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while wet.

If the tank is cracked, or water leaks again after refitting it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

articles.topic: the app not finding the device
articles.text:
Orrin heat pump not appearing in the app

If the app cannot find your Orrin heat pump, start by checking that the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi-Fi.

Try these steps in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Check your phone’s settings and allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access.
3. Turn your phone’s Wi-Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Close the app completely, reopen it and try adding the device again.
5. Check your app store for an update.

If the device still does not appear, contact Halvard Home support. Tell us your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

articles.topic: the app not finding the device
articles.text:
Keel washing machine not found in the app

If the Halvard Home app cannot find your Keel washing machine, start by checking that the machine is switched on and your phone is nearby.

Connect your phone to a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network before adding the machine. A 5 GHz connection will not work for setup. Switch on Bluetooth and allow the app to access nearby devices when prompted.

Close and reopen the app, then try adding the washing machine again. Follow the pairing instructions shown in the app.

If it still does not appear, restart your phone and router, then retry once Wi-Fi is available.

Still having trouble? Contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and a description of where setup stops.

Water leaking underneath your Orrin heat pump

Water beneath the outdoor unit can be normal. During defrosting, ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains away, leaving a puddle underneath.

Check where the water is coming from without removing any covers. If it drains from beneath the outdoor unit during or shortly after defrosting, monitor it to see whether it stops.

Clear loose leaves from around the drainage area, but do not insert tools into the unit or try to chip away ice.

If water runs continuously, comes from a pipe joint or appears beneath an indoor unit, arrange an inspection by a qualified heat pump engineer.

Keep away from wet electrical connections. Contact Halvard Home support if you cannot identify the source safely.

Orrin heat pump heating slowly

Your Orrin heat pump warms your home gradually, so radiators may feel cooler than those connected to a boiler. This does not necessarily mean there is a fault.

If heating seems unusually slow or weak:

- Check that heating mode is selected and the timer allows heating now.
- Set the room thermostat 2°C above the current room temperature to request heat.
- Keep doors and windows closed while the home warms up.
- Check the outdoor unit for leaves or other loose debris blocking airflow. Do not remove covers or touch internal parts.

Cold weather and defrost cycles can temporarily reduce heat output. Avoid repeatedly switching the system off and on.

If performance remains poor, contact Halvard Home support or a qualified heat pump engineer.

Connecting your Fenwick cooker hood to wi-fi

The Fenwick cooker hood connects to a 2.4 GHz home wi-fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.

Before you start, have your wi-fi password ready and connect your phone to the 2.4 GHz network.

1. Switch on the cooker hood at the mains.
2. Open the Halvard Home app on your phone and select **Add appliance**.
3. Choose **Cooker hood**, then follow the app’s instructions to put the hood into pairing mode.
4. Select your home network and enter its password.
5. Keep your phone near the hood until the app confirms the connection.

If pairing fails, check the password and make sure your router’s 2.4 GHz network is enabled, then try again.
